incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Sangbeop), Act No. 1000, as amended, particularly Articles 288, 289, 291, 292, 293, 301, 305, 306, 316, 317, 368, 383, 388, and 434; together with the Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules and the Registration of Commercial Entities and Buildings Regulations
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, Registration Office / local District Court Registration Office within the territorial jurisdiction of the company's registered office, including the electronic I-reg window (Internet Registration of Korea)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Corporation Incorporation Registration (Chusik Hoesa Seolrip Deunggi) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None - Korean law does not prescribe a minimum stated capital for a Chusik Hoesa. However, if the promoters fix a stated capital in the Articles of Incorporation, the full subscription price must be paid into a designated bank account opened in the company's name before the incorporation registration is filed. The bank must issue a capital payment certificate or deposit certificate confirming the receipt of the full subscription funds. There is no statutory minimum amount, but the capital must be genuinely received and the deposit account is effectively blocked until the registration certificate is issued; funds may be released for lawful business purposes after incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR_CHUSIKHOESA ADOPTED IN WRITING ON [EFFECTIVE DATE] AT [REGISTERED OFFICE]. WHEREAS the undersigned are the fully constituted Board of Directors of KR_ChusikHoesa (the Company), a Chusik Hoesa to be incorporated under the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea; and WHEREAS the Commercial Act and the Articles of Incorporation require the Board to address capitalization, banking, registered office and statutory officers at the first sitting; and WHEREAS all directors have agreed to act by unanimous written consent in lieu of an actual meeting in accordance with Article 368 of the Commercial Act and the Company's Articles of Incorporation, the following resolutions are adopted and effective immediately. 1. SUBSCRIPTION AND PAID-IN CAPITAL. The Board accepts the report of the promoters showing that the Company will issue [NUMBER] ordinary shares with a par value of [VALUE] Korean Won each, for aggregate stated capital of [AMOUNT] Korean Won. The Company has received the capital payment certificate issued by [BANK NAME] confirming that every subscriber has paid the full amount of the subscription into the Company's capital subscription account. The Board approves such subscriptions, directs the Company to recognize paid-in capital of [AMOUNT] Korean Won, and directs the representative director to complete the incorporation registration and to cause the paid-in capital to remain fully available only for lawful corporate purposes after the certificate of incorporation is issued. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION. The Board authorizes the opening of corporate operating accounts and digital payment settlement accounts with one or more licensed banks in the Republic of Korea for cash-on-delivery settlement operations. All checks, promissory notes, bank transfer instructions, account opening documents, payment gateway agreements, logistics settlement documents and cross-border remittance forms shall require the joint signature of any two directors among [DIRECTOR A], [DIRECTOR B] and [DIRECTOR C]. The Board authorizes contracting with payment service providers and executing all foreign exchange declarations required under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE. The Board adopts [FULL STREET ADDRESS, CITY, PROVINCE, REPUBLIC OF KOREA] as the registered office of the Company within the jurisdiction of [DISTRICT COURT]. The representative director shall register the address with the competent court registry, display corporate identification, and file all required notices. 4. STATUTORY OFFICERS. The Board appoints [PERSON 1] as Representative Director and Chief Executive Officer, [PERSON 2] as Director and Chief Financial Officer, and [PERSON 3] as Statutory Auditor, each holding office for the term fixed in the Articles of Incorporation. The Representative Director shall have authority to execute all statutory filings and commercial contracts; the Statutory Auditor shall review financial records, internal controls and anti-money-laundering procedures. 5. RATIFICATION AND IMPLEMENTATION. All lawful acts performed by the promoters in the Company's name before this resolution are ratified. The Board directs all officers to take every action required by Korean law to implement this resolution and to report on the completion of incorporation at the next board meeting. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Clearance, Notarization of Articles of Incorporation and Promoter Due Diligence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Supreme Court of Korea, Internet Registration Office (I-reg) at https://www.i-reg.go.kr; Notary Public office or law office located within the jurisdiction of the future registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Perform a preliminary search on the Supreme Court electronic registration system to ensure the proposed Korean trade name of the Chusik Hoesa is not identical to an existing registered company. Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in English and Korean with a precise business purpose covering internet mail-order retail, cash-on-delivery settlement, cross-border trade and logistics. Have each promoter sign the Articles before a notary public and obtain the notarial certification required for Korean commercial registration. If a promoter is located outside Korea, execute a notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favor of a resident formation agent. Keep the notarized Articles ready for use by the bank and the district court registry.
required_dossiers: Proposed Korean trade name and two backup names
Articles of Incorporation draft and final notarized version
Promoter identity documents such as passport or foreigner residence card
I-reg name search confirmation
Power of attorney if a local formation agent is appointed
Certificate of apostille or consular legalization for foreign signatures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name search flags a conflicting mark, submit a second-choice name immediately; if the notary refuses certification because of incomplete identity evidence, supplement the passport, apostille, or consular legalization and resubmit without restarting the statutory filing calendar.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Capital Subscription Deposit Account and Payment of Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Designated commercial bank in the Republic of Korea, such as Kookmin, Shinhan, Woori, or Hana Bank corporate branch, within the jurisdiction of the intended registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The promoters must open a temporary corporate capital subscription account in the company's name at a Korean bank before filing the incorporation registration. The bank will require the notarized Articles of Incorporation, promoter consent, identity documents, a corporate name confirmation, and anti-money-laundering declarations. Each subscriber pays the full subscription price to this account by wire or cash deposit. The bank then issues a capital payment certificate or deposit certificate confirming the receipt of the full subscription amount. If the capital is transferred from abroad, ensure that the inward foreign exchange declaration is reported through the main bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Do not release or withdraw the subscription funds until the incorporation registration is accepted.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Subscriber and promoter identity documents
Corporate name reservation or name search confirmation
Bank account opening application
Anti-money-laundering beneficial ownership declaration
Inward remittance confirmation and foreign exchange declaration if subscription funds come from overseas
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank challenges the beneficial owner documentation, provide a beneficial ownership schedule and certified English translations; if the deposit certificate is refused because of a foreign currency remittance error, file a corrected foreign exchange declaration with the main bank and ask the bank to confirm the credited amount before reissuing the certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Incorporation Registration Filing at the Local District Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registry Office or the District Court with territorial jurisdiction over the registered office; online filing through the Supreme Court I-reg system is accepted
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the incorporation registration application together with the original notarized Articles of Incorporation, capital payment certificate, written consents of directors and statutory auditor, identification documents, corporate seal or seal registration certificate, and proof of payment of registration tax and education tax. Use the statutory form for stock corporation incorporation registration. The court registry verifies the capital receipt, notarial form, board appointments, and corporate purpose. Upon approval, the registry assigns a corporate registration number and issues the certificate of incorporation registration. The date of this registration is the legal formation date of the Chusik Hoesa.
required_dossiers: Original notarized Articles of Incorporation
Capital payment certificate issued by the bank
Written consent of each director and statutory auditor
Incorporation registration application form for a Chusik Hoesa
Registration tax and education tax payment receipts
Corporate seal registration certificate or individual seal impression certificate
Power of attorney for the filing agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a correction or supplementary order, download the deficiency notice from I-reg, correct the specified entries within the court-granted cure period, and refile the amended application. If the statutory fee payment was rejected, print a new remittance slip and attach the proof of payment before re-submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Online Mail-Order Sales Business Report
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office of the National Tax Service and the competent Gu Office of the local municipal government where the registered office is located
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the incorporation certificate is issued, file the business registration application with the National Tax Service under the Value-Added Tax Act, indicating internet mail-order retail, e-commerce, and cash-on-delivery settlement as the principal business. After receiving the business registration certificate, file the Mail-Order Sales Business Report, known as Tongsinsaengeop Singo, with the Gu Office under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce. The report must include the company name, registered address, CEO identity, website or application address, contact information, and consumer dispute-resolution procedures. The Gu Office will issue a report certificate, and the company must display the registration information on its online storefront before commencing cash-on-delivery operations.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Business registration application under the Value-Added Tax Act
Lease contract or certificate of free use for the registered office
CEO identification document
Mail-Order Sales Business Report form
Website or application URL and privacy policy
Consumer dispute settlement procedures and terms of use
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Gu Office delays or rejects the report, produce records proving the registered office and online disclosure; request a written refusal and lodge an administrative appeal with the municipal government within 90 days of the refusal. Do not operate a live cash-on-delivery website until the report certificate is issued.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Activation, COD Settlement Integration and Cross-Border Remittance Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Primary commercial bank in the Republic of Korea and the Ministry of Economy and Finance / Bank of Korea through the designated Main Bank for foreign exchange transactions
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Activate operational corporate bank accounts using the certificate of incorporation and the business registration certificate. Present the first board resolution designating authorized signatories, the corporate seal certificate, and directors' identification. Apply for internet banking, escrow settlement services, and a cash-on-delivery settlement account with the logistics provider. If payment rails include Airwallex or other cross-border payment service providers, verify that the provider operates through a bank licensed in Korea or through an authorized payment institution and record all cash-on-delivery receipts in the authorized settlement account. File the prescribed foreign exchange declarations with the Main Bank for each inbound or outbound remittance, and implement anti-money-laundering controls in customer onboarding and transaction monitoring before accepting live orders.
required_dossiers: Certificate of incorporation registration
Business registration certificate
Board resolution on authorized account signatories
Corporate seal certificate and signatory identification
Anti-money-laundering and beneficial ownership information
Payment service provider agreement or logistics COD settlement confirmation
Foreign exchange transaction report forms for cross-border payments
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If account activation is suspended by the bank's anti-money-laundering committee, respond with source-of-funds evidence, the board resolution, and the commercial operating model file. If the selected payment service provider is not licensed for Korean settlement, replace it with a licensed local payment institution and file all required foreign exchange reports with the Main Bank.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable to an industrial manufacturing license; the competent consumer commerce authority is the local Gu Office together with the National Tax Service. If a physical logistics warehouse is later introduced, add the Ministry of Employment and Labor and the local Fire Department as competent authorities.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Mandatory non-industrial registration: Mail-Order Sales Business Report (Tongsinsaengeop Singo) and Business Registration Certificate for online retail under the Act on Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce. Industrial manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing operating license: Not Applicable for the ISIC 4791 cash-on-delivery e-commerce scope.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Korea and Korea Environment Corporation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Not Applicable for the ISIC 4791 mail-order retail operation because it is neither a manufacturing installation nor an EIA-listed development. A Full Environmental Impact Assessment would apply only if the company later constructs or expands a logistics warehouse facility on a site of 100,000 square meters or more under Article 22 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and its Enforcement Decree.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: N/A - no industrial wastewater, VOC, or hazardous waste discharge is generated by the cash-on-delivery online retail activity. If a sorting center or warehouse is established, the operator must comply with the Clean Water Act and the Waste Management Act for washwater and packaging waste, maintain dry and wet waste segregation, and meet the Ministry of Environment odour and VOC standards for any diesel equipment used on site. No quantitative discharge limit can be assigned to the current e-commerce-only scope.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense fire permit and structural load inspection are Not Applicable to the mail-order office activity. The office must nonetheless satisfy basic fire safety requirements, including portable extinguishers, exit signs, emergency lighting, and automatic fire detection where required by the Fire Safety Installation Act. Occupational clearance: register the workplace with the Ministry of Employment and Labor if regular employees are engaged and provide workplace safety and health training under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. If a warehouse is introduced, obtain a separate Civil Defense fire safety certificate, racking stability inspection, and emergency evacuation plan approval before operations begin.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS). The official electronic portal is the HomeTax system, which is the online channel for tax registration, electronic tax invoice transmission, VAT filing, and issuance of Business Registration Certificates. Export clearance is handled separately by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS portal.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a newly incorporated Chusik Hoesa (stock corporation), the statutory route is: (1) notarize the articles of incorporation and complete any shareholder capital subscriptions, noting that no statutory minimum paid-in capital is required; (2) register the incorporation with the competent District Court under the Korean Commercial Act and obtain the Certificate of Corporation Registration; (3) within 20 days of business commencement, file the Business Registration application with the competent District Tax Office or electronically through the NTS HomeTax system, using the procedures prescribed by the Framework Act on National Taxes and the Value-Added Tax Act; (4) submit the supporting dossier, including the articles of incorporation, Certificate of Corporation Registration, proof of the principal office location (lease agreement or building registration), identity evidence of directors, the corporate seal registration certificate, and the board resolution authorizing the Korean entity; (5) upon verification, the NTS issues the Business Registration Certificate containing the 10-digit Business Registration Number, which is simultaneously the corporate tax identification number, the VAT registration number, and the number required for all tax invoices. For a foreign non-resident seller that has no Korean place of business but makes taxable Korean-destination supplies, including cross-border e-commerce, digital content, or game distribution, the foreign entity must appoint a Korean tax representative under a notarized power of attorney. The tax representative files the Foreign Business Operator VAT Registration application through the NTS HomeTax foreign-registration channel and submits the foreign certificate of incorporation, board resolution, statutes or equivalent constitutional documents, evidence of the Korean payment gateway and local logistics or digital-service use arrangements, and the tax representative's appointment documents. The NTS then issues a Foreign Business Operator VAT identification number, which the foreign seller must quote on any tax invoices and on its Korean VAT filings.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korean national tax law applies mandatory entity-level taxation to a Chusik Hoesa and does not permit US-style check-the-box elections, partnership-style pass-through treatment, or hybrid mismatch entity elections. A Chusik Hoesa cannot be disregarded for Korean corporate income tax or VAT purposes.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No exemption threshold for a Chusik Hoesa: registration is mandatory within 20 days of business commencement regardless of turnover. The simplified taxable person ceiling for certain unincorporated small physical merchants is KRW 80,000,000 of annual taxable turnover, but this simplified status is not available to a stock corporation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea mandates electronic tax invoicing through the NTS HomeTax system for all VAT-registered businesses. Electronic tax invoices must be transmitted to the NTS at issuance, and the HomeTax platform validates the issuer and assignee tax registration data through an API-connected real-time clearance layer. There is no physical paper stamp or independent fiscal seal, but anti-fraud protection operates through mandatory sequentially referenced electronic tax invoice numbers, automatic NTS matching of input and output VAT, mandatory electronic cash receipt issuance for qualifying B2C transactions, and strict denial of input VAT credits for invoices that were not issued, transmitted, or validated through HomeTax. ERP-to-NTS integration is supported by HomeTax API and since-module connectors. Korea therefore has a mandatory digital fiscal clearance record, but not a pre-transaction stamping model.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act, a zero rate applies to supplies of goods exported from Korea, to services rendered to non-residents outside Korea where the place of supply and effective use and enjoyment are outside Korea, and to qualifying international transportation services. For digital content and game exports, the Korean supplier must evidence that the recipient is a non-resident customer located abroad, that the service is supplied and consumed outside Korea, and that the consideration is received through foreign payment rails. For physical e-commerce and mail-order exports settled by cash on delivery, zero rating requires the goods to be physically delivered to a foreign customs jurisdiction under a Korea Customs Service export clearance, followed by foreign exchange repatriation to Korea. In a COD cross-border model, the exporter must preserve the complete transactional chain proving the destination of goods, the foreign buyer identity, and the payment collected overseas and remitted inbound.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration cleared through UNI-PASS and containing the export bill number
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the export declaration
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, or a postal/EMS dispatch record for small-value parcel exports
Bank-issued Inward Remittance Certificate or Foreign Exchange Remittance Confirmation under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
Export sales contract or overseas buyer purchase order
Proof of final overseas delivery, such as foreign customs entry evidence, delivery confirmation, or logistics event trace for the destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly audit export zero-rating through cross-matching of UNI-PASS declarations, transport and parcel tracking records, payment gateway settlement data, and bank foreign-exchange receipts. If zero-rated export supplies are found to be fictitious, unsupported, diverted to the domestic Korean market, or not settled through qualified foreign exchange repatriation within the statutory 180-day deadline, the zero rating is retrospectively annulled and the supply is reclassified as taxable domestic supply. The NTS will assess output VAT at 10%, plus negligence surcharges under the Framework Act on National Taxes, fraudulent understatement penalties of up to 40% of the unpaid VAT, and interest. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act separately imposes penalty surcharges and administrative fines for unrepatriated export proceeds, and confirmed export VAT fraud or issuance of false electronic tax invoices is subject to criminal referral under Korean tax evasion statutes. The statutory assessment period for these clawback adjustments applies for the standard national tax audit window, during which the taxpayer must retain the complete documentation bundle listed above.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a free-market current account with no mandatory conversion of export earnings to KRW; however, all capital account movements and certain current account settlements must be reported to the Bank of Korea under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Profit remittance by a foreign-invested Chusik Hoesa is generally permitted after verification of paid-in capital, retained earnings, tax clearance, and statutory audit where required, but remittances above USD 500,000 must be filed with the foreign exchange bank and may require additional supporting documentation. Non-resident shareholders may convert KRW dividends into foreign currency without prior approval provided the underlying investment was registered and the remittance is within the confirmed earnings base. Capital account items, including inbound equity injections and outbound loans, are subject to prior notification or approval thresholds. The Korean won is convertible for trade and ordinary business transactions, but speculative flows are curtailed by real demand documentation, certificate of deposit rules, and one-time registration requirements. Exchange rates are determined under a market average system, and banks may provide local and foreign currency accounts without statutory surrender ratio.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, export proceeds must be collected within 18 months from the export performance date; there is no mandatory surrender ratio to local currency, but the proceeds must be deposited with a foreign exchange bank and the conversion to KRW may be made at the bank's announced customer exchange rate. Failure to collect within the statutory deadline requires Bank of Korea approval or an extension.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Viability is low for offshore digital EMIs such as Airwallex as a primary account because they are not licensed banks under the Korean Banking Act and cannot hold customer deposits in KRW or open foreign investment registered accounts. They may serve only as ancillary FX collection and disbursement rails if they operate through a licensed domestic bank partnership; domestic regulatory reporting must still be executed by the Korean bank. Therefore, an entity should not rely on a standalone fintech EMI for statutory capital verification or trade settlement reporting.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Chusik Hoesa controlled by non-resident directors, Korean banks generally require the statutory director or an authorized signatory to attend an in-branch interview before account activation. Remote opening through a consular proxy is permitted under certain banks if the power of attorney is notarized by the Korean embassy or consulate and apostilled, but enhanced due diligence for medium-risk COD merchants may still trigger a physically observed video KYC and a face-to-face meeting or local agent verification. There is no blanket statutory mandate requiring personal appearance, yet bank policy frequently treats this as compulsory for non-resident UBOs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership attribution gap for non-resident shareholders of the Chusik Hoesa.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified list of ultimate shareholders through each corporate layer, notarized and apostilled passports, foreign corporate registry extracts, UBO declaration under the Act on Real Name Financial Transactions, and a sworn affidavit of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-on-delivery settlement model creating high volumes of unstructured cash and agent-collected receipts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed logistics and COD collection contracts with licensed couriers, daily cash reconciliation statements through POS and escrow bank accounts, merchant settlement reports, an auditable trail from order to bank deposit, and internal AML transaction monitoring procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistency between offshore digital content sales and domestic cash-on-delivery revenue pattern.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sales invoices and tax proof, VAT-exempt export evidence where applicable, platform payout reports, customer receipts from domestic and offshore channels, revenue recognition policies, and audited financial statements.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Suspected shell structure with minimal operational substance despite anticipated high transaction throughput.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan, board meeting minutes, office lease certificate, payroll and social insurance filings, prior year corporate tax filings, pro-forma cash flow projections, and verified records of physical operational premises.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity must be notified or approved under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; funds should be routed via SWIFT to a foreign currency registered account at a licensed Korean bank using the FDI purpose code, then transferred to a KRW account and converted after the bank issues a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate or capital verification. The investor must submit a capital investment declaration, UBO documentation, and proof of source of funds before the bank releases the capital for business use.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for open account settlements, commercial letters of credit for documentary trade, and documentary collections for low-risk settlement; all payments must be reported to the Bank of Korea through the domestic settlement bank, with FX transaction reports submitted within the statutory period. Logistics remittance for COD is routed through the domestic merchant account to local couriers and offshore partners under a closed-loop treasury architecture.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Licensed KRW/USD forward contracts with domestic commercial banks limited to genuine trade and cash-flow exposure
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) executed through offshore banks only when the counterparty demonstrates underlying Korean won exposure and settlement is in reserve currencies
FX currency swaps and cross-currency swaps with Korean banks for capital account exposures such as foreign currency loans, subject to MOEF/BOK notification
Plain-vanilla FX options used with forwards for hedging, while speculative layered option strategies are prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual general meeting of shareholders and approval of statutory financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate records at the registered office; director changes are filed with the local District Court Registry under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, no later than March 31 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the AGM exposes the company to criminal negligence fines and invalidates formal shareholder approval of financial statements; failure to register re-elected or new directors within 14 days after the resolution triggers a negligence penalty under the commercial registration rules, and a company that abandons its registered office or fails to maintain contact ability for legal process may face court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return with financial statements and tax adjustments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year-end; for a December 31 year-end, due March 31 with extension to the next business day if the date falls on a weekend or public holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of unpaid corporate income tax if filed after the deadline and 20% if not filed, plus 0.022% daily overdue interest on unpaid tax; repeated non-filing for more than one year and absence of active business operations may trigger administrative closure of the business registration by the tax authority, which is the Korean administrative strike-off equivalent.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local income tax on corporate income return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Competent local government tax office under the Local Tax Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same as the corporate income tax return; for a December 31 year-end, due March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of up to 20% of the local tax due plus daily overdue interest and collection enforcement by attachment or seizure of corporate assets; habitual non-filing can lead to cancellation of the business registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Semi-annual value-added tax settlement return and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: First half of the fiscal year (January-June): due July 25; second half (July-December): due January 25 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional VAT assessment of at least 10% on unpaid or underdeclared output VAT plus daily interest for non-payment; continued non-filing permits the tax office to deem the business dormant and administratively close the business registration.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Korea imposes progressive national corporate income tax brackets of 9% (up to KRW 200 million), 19% (KRW 200 million - 20 billion), 21% (KRW 20-300 billion), and 24% (over KRW 300 billion), plus a 10% local income tax surcharge on the national tax, producing a top combined effective marginal rate of 26.4%. Incentive regimes include 100% corporate tax holidays for up to 5 years (and 50% for a further 2 years) for qualifying high-technology or foreign-invested enterprises in Free Economic Zones, R&D and employment tax credits up to approximately 30% for SMEs, investment tax credits for automation and logistics facilities, and an intellectual-property income deduction for Korean-developed patented technology.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return for Computation of Taxable Income and Tax Amount (CIT Form), filed electronically through the National Tax Service HomeTax portal (www.hometax.go.kr) with financial statements and mandatory attachment schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; semi-annual intermediate prepayments are made during the fiscal year and settled at the annual filing.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, the return must be filed by March 31 of the following year, and a corporation may apply for an extension of up to 45 days with the district tax office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total taxable income of the Korean domestic corporation after reconciling book net income to the corporate income tax base through statutory adjustments, limitations, disallowances, and tax-free reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean-resident Chusik Hoesa declares worldwide income; the non-resident parent's income is not consolidated. All cross-border payments to the parent, including COD logistics fees, Airwallex settlement charges, and local remittance costs, must be deducted only at arm's length amounts before arriving at this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1b - Computed corporate income tax amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The progressive national corporate income tax calculated by applying the 9%, 19%, 21%, and 24% statutory brackets to the taxable income in Box 1a.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entity must separately report the 10% local income tax surcharge on the local tax return; non-resident shareholders cannot claim this local surcharge as a foreign tax credit, and most DTAs do not credit it.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule of related-party transactions with foreign parties
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of all transactions with foreign related parties, including the non-resident parent, covering COD payment settlement, logistics service fees, interest on intercompany loans, royalties, and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Mandatory when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions reach or exceed KRW 5 billion. The Korean entity must disclose the transfer pricing method, the arm's length price, and the economic substance (personnel, assets, functions, and risks) that support the compensation paid to the foreign parent, and must maintain a Local File for NTS inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Schedule of payments to non-residents and withholding declarations
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report of every dividend, interest, royalty, and service fee paid to a non-resident payee during the fiscal year, together with the withholding tax remitted to the government.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For each outbound payment to the non-resident parent or beneficiary, the Korean entity must verify that a valid Tax Residency Certificate and beneficial-ownership declaration was received before payment; if not, the full statutory effective WHT of 22% must be withheld and remitted to the National Tax Service, and treaty rate relief is denied.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Foreign tax credit and tax reduction/exemption schedule
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claims for foreign tax credits, statutory tax deductions, DTA-based reductions, and special SME or investment incentives.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Korean resident entity may only claim foreign tax credits for foreign branch income or foreign-source income properly taxable in Korea; the entity must not claim credits for withholding taxes that the non-resident parent is entitled to claim in its own residence jurisdiction, and any treaty reduction on Korean dividend WHT must be documented with the parent's TRC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-filing of the annual CIT return triggers an additional penalty of 20% of the unpaid tax under Article 47 of the Framework Act on National Taxes; fraudulent omission or false understatement attracts a 40% additional charge, negligent understatement attracts 10%, and unpaid tax accrues daily delinquency interest of approximately 0.022% per day (about 8% per annum); the National Tax Service may impose compulsory collection and criminal prosecution of up to 5 years imprisonment plus fines up to 3 times the evaded tax under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% national statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Korean resident corporation to a non-resident, plus 10% local surcharge on the WHT, for an effective statutory rate of 22%; most Korean DTAs reduce the rate to 5%-10% for substantial shareholdings and 10%-15% for portfolio investors.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must deliver a Tax Residency Certificate issued by its home tax authority, complete the Korean treaty relief application on HomeTax, submit a beneficial-ownership declaration confirming the recipient is the true legal and economic owner and not a conduit entity, and provide substance documentation; the Korean payer files the reduced-withholding return and remits the tax by the 10th day of the following month, while the NTS may deny treaty benefits under Korean GAAR if the main purpose of the arrangement is treaty shopping.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on cross-border interest and royalties is 20% national WHT plus 2% local surcharge, for a 22% effective rate; treaty rates commonly reduce interest to 0%-10% and royalties to 0%-15% (typically 10%), but relief requires contemporaneous TRC, beneficial-ownership proof, and an arm's length transfer pricing analysis of the underlying intercompany debt and intangible licensing arrangement.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when aggregate foreign related-party transactions are at least KRW 5 billion for the fiscal year; Master File is mandatory when the aggregate reaches KRW 50 billion; a reduced threshold of KRW 3 billion applies to related parties in designated tax-haven jurisdictions, and documentation must be submitted to the NTS within 30 days of a request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not maintain a separate labeled ESR statute but enforces a functional equivalent through substance-over-form principles, the corporate residence rules of the Corporate Income Tax Act, and CFC and GAAR provisions of the Adjustment of International Taxes Act; a Korean Chusik Hoesa must maintain real local premises, employees, books, management decision-making, and control over COD logistics and payment settlement, because if Core Income-Generating Activities are performed in Korea yet attributed to the foreign parent, the NTS may recharacterize the parent as a Korean permanent establishment, reallocate e-commerce profit to Korea, deny treaty benefits, and impose TP corrections and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Chusik Hoesa collects COD proceeds from logistics and remittance agents but deliberately omits these cash settlements from VAT and corporate income tax books, issues false reconciliation statements, and files a fabricated corporate tax return to suppress taxable income for the foreign parent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 9 and 10 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, intentional tax evasion is punishable by imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine up to 2-3 times the evaded tax; civil additional charges include a 40% fraudulent-return negligence surcharge, a 20% non-filing surcharge, and daily delinquency interest of about 8% per annum.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced: a director who ordered or benefited from the concealment is jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, VAT, surcharges, and interest; the director is blacklisted as a serious delinquent taxpayer, published with the tax deficiency, placed under an overseas travel ban, and faces criminal imprisonment and personal asset restitution to the National Tax Service.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax Failure on Outbound Profit Repatriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The Korean entity pays dividends, interest, or COD-software royalties to the non-resident parent without withholding the statutory WHT, fails to file HomeTax withholding returns, does not obtain the parent's Tax Residency Certificate, or disguises profit distributions as inflated logistics and commission fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The entity as statutory withholding agent is held liable for the full unwithheld amount plus a 30% non-payment additional charge and daily delinquency interest; treaty relief is denied because the TRC and beneficial-ownership protocol was not satisfied, and criminal penalties apply if the transaction is fraudulent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and de facto representatives who signed the remittance instructions are secondarily liable for the unwithheld tax under the Framework Act on National Taxes; the NTS may attach their personal assets, place them on the departure-restriction blacklist for unpaid tax above the statutory threshold, and pursue criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Treaty-Shopping Economic Substance Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The foreign parent establishes or uses a letterbox Korean Chusik Hoesa with no office, no staff, no local management, and no independent COD logistics or payment settlement contracts, solely to route e-commerce revenue to a low-tax jurisdiction and to claim DTA benefits or tax haven treatment for Korean-source income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Korean GAAR and the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, the NTS may deny treaty benefits, reject the Tax Residency Certificate application, recharacterize the arrangement, impose transfer pricing understatement penalties of 15%-30% of the adjusted taxable income, and add daily delinquency interest; the foreign parent can be taxed as a Korean permanent establishment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Resident directors are personally liable for the reassessed tax and penalties, with the corporate veil pierced to attach personal bank accounts and real estate; directors are blacklisted and travel-restricted, must restore transferred assets to the tax authority, and face criminal prosecution for aiding tax evasion, including imprisonment for up to 5 years.
